info.title: i2 Analyze REST API
info.description:
Welcome to the documentation for the i2 Analyze REST API.

At this version, the REST API provides the ability to run text and geospatial searches against the data in the Information Store; to download schemas and server settings; and to perform some server administration functions.

As well as reading the content here, you can click **Download OpenAPI spec** to retrieve the API specification in JSON format.

# Experimental methods

At this version of the API, the search and record group endpoints are _experimental_. That means they're fully functional, but i2 reserves the right to change the names or structures of the APIs outside the usual deprecation cycle.

To use these methods, you must acknowledge this behavior by adding the `I2-Experimental-Apis` HTTP header to all requests. For more information, see the documentation in the **Search** and **Record Groups** sections.

# RFC 7807

The i2 Analyze server provides error responses that conform to [RFC 7807](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7807). For API methods that support multiple or complex parameters (for example, [`POST /api/v1/infostore/search/text`](#post-/api/v1/infostore/search/text)) these responses contain richer information about the problem that caused the error in a standardized JSON structure.

For more information about the error responses, see the documentation for error responses on the affected methods (for example, HTTP status code 400).


# JSON Web Tokens

i2 Analyze supports a JSON Web Token (JWT) authentication mechanism for third-party integrations. The mechanism is not enabled by default, so you must first [configure it on the i2 Analyze server](https://docs.i2group.com/analyze/jwt-authentication.html).

When the mechanism is enabled, a client that authenticates successfully with the i2 Analyze server receives a cookie containing a JWT token. That cookie is then passed back to the server with subsequent client requests, as well as to any third-party applications that are deployed to the same domain as the i2 Analyze server.

As a result of this arrangement, a third-party application can use the JWT token to make requests to the i2 Analyze server on behalf of the authenticated user, without the user having to provide their credentials to the application. For more information, see [JWT authentication](https://docs.i2group.com/analyze/jwt-authentication.html).


# Common HTTP status codes

The methods in the i2 Analyze REST API return HTTP status codes that indicate the outcome of a method call. The following status codes are common to all the methods in the REST API, and have common interpretations:

- 304: The resource has not been modified since the version specified in the request header.

- 401: "Unauthorized", which actually means unauthenticated.

- 403: Forbidden. The user is authenticated with i2 Analyze but not authorized to use the requested feature.

- 405: The request is for a method that is not supported.

- 406: The requested resource can only generate content that is not acceptable according to the **Accept** headers in the request.

- 415: The request has a media type that the server or resource does not support.

- 500: Internal server error.

As well as the codes in this list, each method in the REST API can return different HTTP status codes in different circumstances. The documentation for each method contains full details when that is the case.

post.summary: Reload the geospatial configuration, match rules, highlight query definitions, visual query configuration, and item type access configuration
post.description:
This method reloads the geospatial configuration, the match rules for Find Matching Records (FMR), the highlight query definitions, the visual query configuration, and the type access configuration from the server settings. Any changes from the existing settings are applied without requiring a server restart.

**Note:** You can use a REST endpoint to reload the _system_ match rules only when the deployment _does not_ include the Information Store. For information on updating the system match rules when the Information Store is present, see the [i2 Analyze documentation](https://docs.i2group.com/analyze/creating_smr_is.html).

500.description: One or more of the configuration files failed validation.

get.summary: Fetch the highlight query configuration that the i2 Analyze server generates
get.description: This method fetches the example highlight query configuration that the i2 Analyze server generates automatically for the current schema, in XML format.

get.summary: Fetch the XSD that can validate highlight query configurations
get.description: This method fetches the XML schema definition that you can use to help create and validate highlight query configurations for the current i2 Analyze schema.

post.summary: Reloads the index configuration from disk.
post.description: **/admin/indexes/config/reload** reloads the index configuration from disk. Any changes from the existing settings are applied without requiring a server restart.

204.description: The POST method completed successfully and the configuration was reloaded.

post.summary: Requeue batches of ingested data that failed indexing
post.description: This method requeues batches of ingested data that failed indexing, after action has been taken to correct problems.

202.description: Failed batches were queued for indexing and removed from the list of failures.

204.description: There were no failed batches to queue.

get.summary: Fetch summary status information about all the indexes that the i2 Analyze server uses
get.description: This method fetches summary status information about all the indexes that the i2 Analyze server uses.

post.summary: Clears the specified index, which then repopulates automatically.
post.description:
**/admin/indexes/{name}/clean** clears all information from the specified index, which then repopulates automatically. See notes on individual parameters below.

This request can take some time to complete. It waits for the application to complete any operations that are populating the index before it takes effect.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the index to clear.

400.description: The index name is unknown to the server.

post.summary: Repopulates the specified index from its data source, starting at the specified point in time.
post.description: **/admin/indexes/{name}/reindex** repopulates the specified index to reflect data source changes since the specified point in time. Existing data in the index is overwritten but not removed. See notes on individual parameters below.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the index to update.

requestBody.description: The timestamp to reindex the data from.

400.description: The request was not formatted correctly or the index name was unknown to the server.

post.summary: Repopulates the specified index from its data source.
post.description: **/admin/indexes/{name}/repopulate** repopulates the specified index from its data source. Existing data in the index is overwritten but not removed - use **/admin/indexes/{name}/clean** to clear and rebuild the index entirely. See notes on individual parameters below.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the index to repopulate.

202.description: The POST request was accepted and will run as soon as possible.

400.description: The index name is unknown to the server.

get.summary: Fetches detailed status information about the specified index.
get.description: **/admin/indexes/{name}/status** fetches detailed status information about the specified index. See notes on individual parameters below.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the index to report on.

post.description:
This method disables the creation of server metrics.

**Note:** Disabling server metrics this way is temporary. The server reverts to its original settings after a restart. To disable metrics permanently, update the server configuration.

This method enables the creation of server metrics.

**Note:** Enabling server metrics this way is temporary. The server reverts to its original settings after a restart. To enable metrics permanently, update the server configuration.

This method disables privacy agreements so that they are not presented to users.

**Note:** Disabling privacy agreements this way is temporary. The server reverts to its original settings after a restart. To disable privacy agreements permanently, update the server configuration.

This method enables privacy agreements so that they are presented to users.

**Note:** Enabling privacy agreements this way is temporary. The server reverts to its original settings after a restart. To enable privacy agreements permanently, update the server configuration.

post.summary: Reset the privacy agreement acceptance state of all users
post.description: This method resets the privacy agreement acceptance state of all users, so that they must all accept the agreement again when they next connect to the server.

post.summary: Set the period after which users must accept the privacy agreement again
post.description:
This method sets the period after which a user who has accepted the privacy agreement must read and accept it again.

**Note:** Setting the acceptance period this way is temporary. The server reverts to its original settings after a restart. To set the acceptance period permanently, update the server configuration.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: The number of days after which users must accept the agreement again. If this parameter is not present, users are not prompted again until the mechanism is reset.

post.summary: Reload the user and group provisioning configuration files and trigger provisioning
post.description: This method reloads the user and group provisioning configuration files and triggers provisioning. Any changes from the existing settings are applied without requiring a server restart.

400.description: One or more of the configuration files failed validation.

post.summary: Reload the security schema, including dimension values from providers
post.description: This method reloads the security schema, which includes reloading dimension values from all the providers specified in the security schema file. After the reload, the full set of security dimension definitions including any dynamically loaded dimension values is available from the **/core/securityschema** endpoint.

delete.summary: Delete all the chartlets in the system.
delete.description: This method deletes all the chartlets in the system.

post.summary: Create and send an alert to the specified set of users
post.description:
This method creates and sends an alert to the specified set of users. See notes on individual parameters below, but also be aware of the following details.

In the request object, the **sendTo** object that you provide must contain at least one field. Users receive the alert if they match any field. For example, if the criteria are:

```json
{
  "userPrincipalNames": ["user1"],
  "groups": ["groupA", "groupB"]
}
```

then a user with the principal name **user1** matches regardless of group membership, and a user who is a member of **groupA** matches regardless of membership of **groupB** (or any other group).

**Note:** A user must have logged into the system before an alert can be sent to them.

requestBody.description: The contents of the alert, and the criteria that define its recipients.

value.title: For your information
value.message: Take a look at this link

value.title: Records added!
value.message: New records added from example source

get.summary: Fetch the i2 Analyze security schema and a set of security dimension values for the current user
get.description: This method fetches the security schema from the i2 Analyze server, together with a set of security dimension values that will be assigned by default to all records that the current user creates.

get.summary: Fetch a list of time zones according to the client's locale
get.description: This method fetches the time zones that the i2 Analyze server supports, formatted according to the locale of the caller.

get.summary: Fetch the version information for the product
get.description:
This method fetches version information for the i2 Analyze deployment.

**Note:** Requests to this endpoint do not require authentication.

post.summary: Reload the cache of gateway and connector data with up-to-date information
post.description:
This method reloads gateway and connector information into the cache on the i2 Analyze server so that clients can use it to make requests to services correctly.

Be aware that in some circumstances, calling this method can result in configuration settings failing to load for a connector that was previously in a valid state.

**Note:** This method is not available on i2 Analyze servers that do not include the i2 Connect gateway.

200.description: The POST method completed successfully and the cache of gateway and connector information was updated.

get.summary: Test that the i2 Analyze server is functioning normally
get.description:
This method tests that the appropriate database and search index components are up and running, and that the server is healthy and handling requests.

**Note:** Requests to this endpoint do not require authentication.

200.description: The application is **up** and handling requests.

503.description: The application is **down** and not handling requests.

get.description: This method fetches the Information Store schema in JSON format.

post.summary: Search for records in the Information Store that meet the specified geospatial criteria
post.description:
This method searches for records in the Information Store that meet the specified geospatial criteria.

**Experimental:** This is a preview of functionality that is subject to change without notice. To use the API, you must opt in by specifying this HTTP header: `I2-Experimental-Apis: SEARCH_V1`.

requestBody.description: The area over which to perform the search.

200.description: The search was successful but no matches were found.

201.description: The search was successful and a record group was created.

post.summary: Search for records in the Information Store that contain the specified terms
post.description:
This method searches for records in the Information Store that contain the specified terms in supported property values or notes. The supported value types for text searches are:

- `SINGLE_LINE_STRING`
- `MULTIPLE_LINE_STRING`
- `SUGGESTED_FROM`
- `SELECTED_FROM`

You can also search for values of other some types by formatting the terms correctly:

- For `DATE` values, use `2020-12-31`
- For `TIME` values, use `12:34:56` (UTC)
- For `DATE_AND_TIME` values, use `2020-12-31T12:34:56Z` (UTC)

Values of other types are not supported in free text searches.

**Experimental:** This is a preview of functionality that is subject to change without notice. To use the API, you must opt in by specifying this HTTP header: `I2-Experimental-Apis: SEARCH_V1`.

requestBody.description: The expression to search for, and optionally the constraints to apply.

200.description: The search was successful but no matches were found.

201.description: The search was successful and a record group was created.

delete.description:
This method deletes the specified record group from the i2 Analyze server.

**Experimental:** This is a preview of functionality that is subject to change without notice. To use the API, you must opt in by specifying this HTTP header: `I2-Experimental-Apis: SEARCH_V1`.

parameters.name: recordGroupId
parameters.description: The identifier of the record group to delete.

400.description: The request did not specify a record group.

404.description: The specified record group does not exist or has expired.

get.summary: Fetch the records in the specified record group, one page at a time
get.description:
This method fetches the records in the specified record group with a forward-only iterator. The initial response contains a single page of records. Any records to which the user no longer has access are not fetched.

**Note:** On any given page, the ends of a link always appear before the link that requires them. If those ends did not match the search, the page can contain more records than specified by `pageSize`. Furthermore, the same record can appear on several pages (but never twice on the same page). Finally, a record group that you iterate through for a second time can contain different records from those it had first time around.

In the response, the `matchedRecordIds` field indicates whether a record is present because it matched the search, or it simply satisfies a link end. If more pages of results are available, the `nextPage` field provides the cursor and a link for the next page. If the number of records in the record group is an exact multiple of `pageSize`, the last page of results can be empty.

**Experimental:** This is a preview of functionality that is subject to change without notice. To use the API, you must opt in by specifying this HTTP header: `I2-Experimental-Apis: SEARCH_V1`.

parameters.name: recordGroupId
parameters.description: The identifier of the record group from which to fetch records.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The position in the record group from which to start retrieving records. The cursor value appears in the response to a previous request. `*` is the cursor for the first record.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description:
The number of _matching_ records to fetch for this page. Defaults to 500 if not supplied.

The ends of a link always appear on the same page as that link, so a page of *N* matching link records can also contain up to 2*N* entity records.

200.description: The page of records was retrieved successfully.

400.description: The request did not specify a record group; or the specified time zone, cursor, or page size was not valid.

404.description: The specified record group does not exist or has expired.

get.summary: Fetch information about the specified user
get.description:
This method fetches information about the specified user.

**Note:** When the specified user is not the current user, the **commandPermissions** array in the response is always empty.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: The principal name of the user to retrieve information about.

404.description: The specified user was not found.

post.summary: Fetch a REST API version that is compatible with the specified version
post.description:
This method fetches a REST API version that the i2 Analyze server supports, and that is compatible with the version that the client specified. See notes on individual parameters below.

If the server does not support a compatible API version, the client receives information that it can use to try a different version or to inform the caller that an update is necessary.

requestBody.description: Information about a REST API version that the client supports.

200.description: The POST method completed successfully, the server supports the requested API version, and the response provides additional detail.

400.description: The request was not formatted correctly.

404.description: The server is older than the client and does not support the requested API version. You must update the server or target an earlier API version.

410.description: The server is newer than the client and no longer supports the requested API version. You must update to a client that targets a supported API version.

I2RFC7807ProblemDetails.description:
An error response generated by the i2 Analyze server. Errors of this type are intended for developers rather than users.

The `errors` extension might provide error messages and other information relating to a specific problem. The `requestId` extension is a randomly generated identifier for the request that can be used to locate corresponding messages in the server logs.

type.description: An absolute URI that identifies the problem type, which must be `tag:i2group.com,2022:problem-details`.

requestId.description: The request identifier UUID, which can be used to locate corresponding messages in the server logs.

errors.description: An optional list of errors that might provide additional details about the cause of the problem.

I2RFC7807UserProblemDetails.description:
An error response generated by the i2 Analyze server. Errors of this type are intended to be displayed to users.

The `errors` extension might provide error messages and other information relating to a specific problem. The `requestId` extension is a randomly generated identifier for the request that can be used to locate corresponding messages in the server logs.

type.description: An absolute URI that identifies the problem type, which must be `tag:i2group.com,2022:user-problem-details`.

requestId.description: The request identifier UUID, which can be used to locate corresponding messages in the server logs.

errors.description: An optional list of errors that might provide additional details about the cause of the problem.

The operational state that this index is currently in. A live index may be `LIVE` or `FAILED`. A standby index can be `DISABLED`, `BUILDING`, `FAILED`, or `READY`.
The `FAILED` state is entered when all batches have been processed, but one or more batches contained invalid data.

**true** if one or more batches of ingested data failed indexing; **false** otherwise.

The **populationProgress** cannot reach 100% while this field is **true**. You must fix and re-ingest the data, and then use the `/api/v1/admin/indexes/retryfailed` endpoint to try indexing again.

I2-Experimental-Apis.name: I2-Experimental-Apis
I2-Experimental-Apis.description:
This header allows you to access experimental APIs. In a request to an experimental API, provide this header with a value that matches the one specified in the `x-i2-api.experimental-token` extension. For example, requests to an endpoint with

```
"x-i2-api": {
  "since": "1.0",
  "experimental": true,
  "experimental-token": "FOO"
}
```

should set `I2-Experimental-Apis: FOO` as a header.
